utterances.text: I think so, but I don't know. I didn't pay much attention to that. I was looking at Mitar because he was obviously in great pain. I know that that man, Savic came, that he drove that ambulance. Whether somebody else was with him, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you helped somebody, I presume the driver, to put him in the ambulance car?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who else was there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. There was Djordje Brusavic [phoen] who is now the principal of my school, and somebody else. But I simply don't remember who else. I know the two of us, that is why we got together, that is why I remember. Who else was there, I just don't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe how is it that you took him into the ambulance in view of all that pain and, as you say, his moans?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, whichever way we tried to turn him, whichever way -- wherever we touched him, he was all right, but when we tried to touch his leg, then he would really cry out loudly, and my neighbour who was up there told me that the true pain started later on. And he really cried when they got him to the X-ray because he had to take off his shoes or, rather, I think it was some boots that he had on. And it hurt him terribly. And a neighbour told me how he unlaced those boots, took out the laces, and they didn't really know how to manage it, how to get this boot off because he was in such great pain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that this street is at a certain slope towards the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell us, what was the weather like, if you remember it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There was nobody in the street. There was some drizzle so that the pavement was wet and the horse, I don't remember what colour exactly it was, but it was dark because even the horse was wet. And Mitar was wet, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you -- we're talking about the horse. Do you remember if that horse had a saddle, bridle or something?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, all he had was some reins. Well, I don't know much about horses. He had a rope or something that he held, but no saddle or anything like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if I explained the reins or is it the bridle that you put in horse's mouth, or rather the bit that you put in the mouth, but nothing else and some rope?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, he had. So he had a tether, a rope, and I don't think he had a bit or anything. I do not think he -- there was anything, no saddle. I don't really know much about horses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what colour was that horse and how tall?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Not very tall, and they called it -- I learned about those horses in school. They called him Bosnian mountain horse, and I think that must have been one of those horses. I live in the town, so I don't see very many horses around, but it was rather dark, a dark brown or something. I don't remember because it was wet, so it was quite dark, but I know it was a dark-coloured horse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to that horse afterwards?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't. The horse stood there for a while as if hypnotized, and as soon as the ambulance car arrived, we, of course, went back into the hotel because there was this drizzle, so that I don't know what happened to the horse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember there where it happened, did you see any other objects, was anything found there?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, there was nothing there. I don't remember. No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was a megaphone, a loud speaker found there or seen thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't see one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard that Mr. Vasiljevic had gone to Uzice?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him around afterwards or not?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I saw him walking through town with crutches. I didn't talk to him. I assumed he was angry with me because it was because of me that he broke his leg, so we just said hello, but I didn't stop to chat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago when I asked you how Mr. Vasiljevic was dressed, I don't think I asked you, although you did write this -- did he have a light coat with him or on him?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't. He was wearing a dark suit, a jacket and trousers, I know that it was of a darker colour, and he was wearing boots and I learnt from the doctor -- I realise this because I learnt from the doctor that he had trouble taking the boots off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about a hat?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. I know Mitar and he never wore a hat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were at the hotel, put up at the hotel. Now, while you were on duty, or perhaps you happened to know from someone else, do you know whether Mr. Vasiljevic at any time or in any way would come in front of the Visegrad Hotel or enter the Visegrad Hotel in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: While I was there, I did not see him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw him on some other occasion, wherever that was, was he wearing a uniform? Did he have a weapon of any kind?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't in uniform and he wasn't carrying a weapon of any kind. And my wife, if I can add that, said, "Well, thanks to him, the town is clean, so I take my hat off to him for that."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you know who assigned him to do that work?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think that somebody assigned him, but who assigned him, I don't know. I wasn't interested in learning about that. But judging by the comments made by the Visegrad population, they were satisfied with the work he was doing and they were satisfied that somebody had been assigned to do that kind of work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about the red arm band a moment ago or ribbon, can I ask you what you thought that band or ribbon represented? To you, what message did it convey to you?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, in our parts, when somebody puts a band on, it means he has been assigned to do some duty work, and at school, when we went to school, when I went to school, we would get these bands or ribbons when somebody was a monitor on duty or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you learn that Mr. Vasiljevic had been arrested and who did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember when the news flashed around town that Mitar had been arrested. I think I saw him on that particular day, actually, but we learnt about it only in the evening, and people said that his wife didn't know where he was and she called Prelaz. As it's a small town, news travels fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your comment when you heard about it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, my comment was, on the basis of what people said, that it was a mistake. People were saying that it was a mistake and that they might have mixed him up with Mitar the Chetnik. That was this man's nickname, but I didn't know that person, Mitar the Chetnik. But everybody said in town that it was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When they mentioned this man Mitar the Chetnik, did they say what he had done, whether he had done anything? How did they mention him, in what context?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he said that he must have done something because I moved around town, parts of town, that I didn't know what was happening in town, so I could just rely on the comments that I heard. And this man had done something in retribution. I don't know the history of Visegrad much because I'm not from Visegrad myself, but he was taking revenge for something. He left Visegrad, actually. His family went off somewhere, and they wanted revenge from the previous war because they were slaughtered; their family was slaughtered during the Second World War. So that this man had come -- I don't know. The man drank a lot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that you don't know that man, Mitar the Chetnik.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I might have seen him but I didn't know what he looked like, who he was because it's a -- but it's a small town so I might have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said that you know Mr. Mitar Vasiljevic as a co-citizen and as a worker and so on. Do you think, in view of knowing Mr. Vasiljevic the way you do, do you think he was capable of doing something which would bring him before this Tribunal, which would merit that he be brought before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so, because he was always -- we would always joke when we met each other. I don't frequent catering establishments much, but when I registered my car which I had bought - it was an imported car - he translated something that had to be translated from German and he didn't want to accept any payment for that. That was a service he did for me, so he was always nice to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TANASKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honour, I hope that I stuck to the time limit and I was more efficient with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There was no time limit but you certainly were more efficient, if I may say so. Cross-examination, yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mitrovic, my name is Dermot Groome and I will be representing the Office of the Prosecutor this afternoon and asking you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what part of Visegrad town do you live in?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I live in the northern part of Visegrad, which means to say the part from the hotel northwards, opposite the hotel, in fact. As it's a small town, let me say that it's opposite. The hotel is in the south and I lived in the northern part of town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And approximately how long would it take you to you walk from your home to the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: As I work in the gym, there's a gym across the road from the hotel, so it takes seven or eight minutes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell us today that during this time period, you were living in the hotel as part of the reserve police force; is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you explain for us the reason for living in the hotel when your own home was just, as you say, seven minutes' walk away?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I was the reserve -- a reservist in the police force and we were in charge of providing security for communication, that is to say, we had points, checkpoints, at the entrance to town. We would control the comings and goings to and from town to ensure that nothing amiss happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately how many checkpoints altogether you manned in town or had in town?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I was deployed in the hotel, and it was my job to make the schedules whereas the checkpoints were -- I can't tell you exactly, but they were roughly in front of every bridge underneath the dam, the electric power plant of Visegrad towards Uzice at the petrol pump. Then there was one towards the subtransformer station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I be correct in thinking that every road in and out of town had some type of checkpoint on it?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you wouldn't be wrong. You would be correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would I also be correct in thinking that if I were living there at the time and I tried to cross through a checkpoint, if the police reservists on the checkpoint didn't recognise me, I'd be asked to produce my identity papers? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, but we all knew each other so there wasn't the need for any strict controls, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were deployed at the hotel itself. Was that just this day or during the -- your entire work during this period were you deployed at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I was in the police station first because it was the beginning, that was at the beginning. And after that, they transferred me to a building near the new bridge, more northerly from my own house. I don't know how long I was there actually, but we were then transferred to the hotel after that. And they would joke with us and say, "Well the situation is like it is and you're staying in a hotel."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you were -- let me ask you this, what time did you begin your duties on this day at the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: We had shifts in the morning and in the evening, so if you had a night shift, for example, as there weren't many of us, then you would rest for 12 hours, you'd be off duty for 12 hours and perhaps you could go home and then have a night shift again, and this would go on for five or six days, because there were only two shifts, either a day shift or a night shift. So it was difficult for us. It was difficult to distribute the people because there weren't many of us. There were very few of us to go around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct in thinking that you were assigned to the day shift as you were in front of the hotel when Mr. Vasiljevic fell off the horse?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I went home in the morning. I wasn't on duty in the shifts like the others. I went home to freshen up because there was no possibility of taking a bath at the hotel, so I came back to the hotel at 3.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at 3.00 p.m., did you remain at the front of the hotel or did you go somewhere else inside the hotel to fulfil your duties?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I was in the hotel and then I stepped outside. I didn't have an assignment, I just went outside. There's an awning in front of the entrance and I stood there alone for a while - I think I was alone - some people were inside. So I like looking at the rain when it was raining.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximate for us how long you were there in front of the hotel before you saw Mr. Vasiljevic fall off the horse?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps 10, 15 minutes. I don't remember exactly. I would go in and come out. Somebody would stop to ask something, but my office or room was upstairs, but we didn't have anything much to do so we were a bit bored and we would roam around that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So according to your estimation, it would have been approximately 3.15 that afternoon that Mr. Vasiljevic fell off the horse?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. No. I came at around 3.00 and went into my room and stayed there half an hour, an hour, I don't remember exactly. Perhaps even two hours went by after I had come back into the hotel, but it was a long time ago so I can't be more specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there's been testimony in this trial that during this period, there were members of White Eagles stationed at that hotel as well as some other men involved in paramilitary activity. During the time you were working with the police reservists, did you see any indication of White Eagles or other paramilitaries either living in or hanging around the Visegrad Hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. I said at the beginning, I think Rade asked me, when we came, there was nobody in the hotel when we arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on this day, prior to seeing Mr. Vasiljevic fall off the horse, did you see any large groups of people congregating in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: That was in the morning. Some people needed two or three buses, I saw that from home. Later on I heard that a convoy was going to Olovo, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: That's what they told me when I arrived at the hotel, and I saw the buses, it's a small place, a small town, you know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the bus company that provided the buses that day?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember. It's a Visegrad company. Now, whether it changed its name, whether it was Centrotrans or Visegradtrans, one or the other. It's Visegradtrans now, but whether -- it's changed its, name but whether it was Centrotrans or Visegradtrans, I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you saying that when you arrived to work that day that the buses were in the square in front of the hotel?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't see the buses. I was at home and somebody, one of the neighbours told my wife that there was a convoy going, and then I went out on to the terrace and saw three buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution document 152. I'm go to ask that the copies be provided to Defence and the Chamber. I'd ask that it be placed on the desk in front of the witness. I think it would be easier for him to make marks on if while it is in front of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I'm just showing you Prosecution document 152. Do you recognise what is depicted in this photograph

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my one here, opposite the hotel, this is the grill, this is the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, can you just tell us now what is depicted in it? I will ask you to make some specific markings to indicate different things that you testified to. Is this a picture of the square in front of the Visegrad hotel that you testified about before us today?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be given a pen, I see some pens there. I would ask that the witness be given the fine point pen. There's a fine point pen in the ELMO, that he be given a blue one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, I would ask you to begin by just writing your name at the bottom of that photograph so we know that it's you that's making markings on it. Mr. Mitrovic, I will ask you to make some marks on it, so I would ask you not to make any marks until instructed to do so, and the first mark I would ask you to make is can you put an X to indicate the spot where you saw Mr. Vasiljevic fall off the horse.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] As this is at an angle, it's roundabout here. Whether it's a metre left or right, I can't quite specify because this photograph has been taken from an angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we be let into the secret and see what it is the witness has done by having it put on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Whereabouts is the X?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: There's an area here where cars are parked on the right. So I don't see how far the street goes. So this X should be a little further over here. I can't orient myself. It's rather a -- there's a lot of light in this photograph shining on the street so I can't actually see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm afraid we're going to have a problem with this because this is quite obviously a photograph taken from a height, from a helicopter, and the building that can be seen at the bottom of the photograph, you can't see what's behind it or rather the parking space that the witness has mentioned. So the square has been hidden by the building at the bottom of the photograph. It doesn't show the square properly, and I don't think this is a useful photograph for identification because you can't actually see the spot from the angle that this photograph has been taken. Perhaps we could find another photograph which shows the whole square because there's a whole part of the square that can't be seen from the building that gets in the way.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: May I say something, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one minute. Mr. Groome, have you got any other photographs or have you got a plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, this is the best photograph that we have of the square from the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Do you have any photographs or a plan, Mr. Domazet?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seem to remember that the Prosecution did have some better photographs of this area, but I'm not quite sure. I can't find them just now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Groome, we're in your hands. I will ask the witness if he's got the answer to it, but it seems to me we're not going to get very far if we can't see the actual point.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I realise there are limitations to this drawing. Hopefully the witness, by qualifying his marks with a description "several metre this way or several metres that way," it may give the Court some kind indication or idea where events happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I have not been through your photographic volume to check, but are there any other photographs of this square?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There are other photographs of the square, Your Honour. This was selected not because -- obviously, I did not know where this man was going to, say, put an X today. It was picked because it was the best picture of the overall square. The most - how should I say - directly above the square. There are other pictures but they are at such extreme angles that very little of the square is visible from overhead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You don't have a photograph that shows the front of the hotel, for example?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we do have a photograph that shows the front of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I understand that's what the witness is trying to say he would be able to show it on better.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't want to quarrel with the Court's interpretation of what the witness said, but I don't believe he's placed the X anywhere near the hotel. If I can ask him to make a few more marks on this, I think it would be clear where the hotel is with respect to the X that he's made and I will look tonight to see if there are other photographs that may show that precise spot that he's indicating for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, before we run out of time, the witness wanted to say something to explain. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On this photograph, I couldn't see Mitar on a horse looking at it from here. This is where I was standing here under this awning and from this area, you -- from this angle, you can't possibly, on the basis of this photograph, see -- this is a catering establishment and it masks the vision. So Mitar was 150 metres away from me, and if I were to draw a line across the photograph from this angle, the corner of this building would prevent me from seeing where he was over here. So you see I should have placed the X more this way. When I placed the X, I saw that I had made a mistake. This is the grill, this is the taxi space. There were no taxis there, parked there at the time. So this is a small tree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrovic, perhaps we can do this. Perhaps -- it seems where you want to change where you've placed the X. Can you put another X where you think it is more -- where you now say you saw him fall off the horse and just put "-2" to so we know where you put the second X and put "-2" to know where the second X is.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Can I -- if that's the raised level where the parking was, can I draw a line there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask that you put a line there and put a "-2" so we know that it's the X that you have.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: If this is the middle of the street, then X-2 would be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we --

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think. Although I'm not quite clear, I can't get my bearings on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's label a few of the buildings so that we all can be oriented to where you are. Are you familiar with a furniture store on the square?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The furniture store is on this corner here. It's a bank now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please put a number --

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: It used to be a furniture store but it's a bank now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please put a number 1 on the roof of the building that you say used to be a furniture store in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: You want number 1?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 1 on the roof of the building that used to be the furniture store. Can you keep it on the desk in front of you, and put a number 2 on the roof of the building that is the UPI terrace grill?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is the terrace of the department store but it's on the ground floor level. There are just some tables outside in front of the tree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where the department store is, can you put a number 5 on the roof of the department store?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that the UPI terrace grill is inside the department store or is that another building?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: The UPI building and the department store and the grill, in front of the grill, there was several tables laid out whereas this is a terrace which you go upstairs to reach it. Can I indicate that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One second now. Can you please put the number 3 on the roof of the Visegrad Hotel and would you please put the initials RS to indicate where is the balcony that Radomir Simsic -- where is Radomir Simsic's apartment?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't think you can see it but it's here abouts, give or take a few metres, NS. Is that what you want?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: RS, please.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: RS, I'm sorry, yes. RS. So I have to rub this out, cross it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that that now be put on the ELMO so the witness can indicate his markings to us.

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Here you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us where you put 1 to indicate where the furniture store was?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you show us where you put 5 to indicate where the department store was?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Number 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put a 3 to indicate where you -- where the Visegrad Hotel is?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: This is the hotel, number 3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you show us where you put RS to indicate an approximation of where Radomir Simsic's house is? And that's just off the bottom edge of the photograph on the street next to the furniture store; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He has also put some dotted lines coming out from that bottom building, which I had thought had been described as the hotel but it is the department store. Is that the raised area that you referred to, sir?

utterances.speaker: PETAR MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's now 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. If you can even compile by reference to photographs some idea of a plan, it may be easier for the witness and for us to follow this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But if you've got any photographs of the inside of the square, I think we should have them. As a matter of curiosity, is the department store leaning over or is that some sort of a visual error?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe he would be able to -- the witness might be able to answer that than myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's out of curiosity, Mr. Groome. We'll resume tomorrow at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: at 4.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m. 25
